questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Updating Dependencies?
options: Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Use parameterized SQL, a managed connection pool, bounded transactions, and reviewed schema migrations.
questions.answer_key: Use parameterized SQL, a managed connection pool, bounded transactions, and reviewed schema migrations.
questions.explanation: Use parameterized SQL, a managed connection pool, bounded transactions, and reviewed schema migrations. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Updating Dependencies?
questions.explanation: “Listing outdated packages” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Updating Dependencies implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
